name: Jeju and Gyeongju, South Korea
regionLabel: A volcanic island and a museum without walls
summary: A lava island for the first week and a tomb-and-temple city for the second. Mild April, excellent for children, less wild than Kyushu's volcano country.
why: Korea is easy with children: food you can share, museums, a volcanic island, and trains. Jeju keeps the nature. Gyeongju gives the 12- and 14-year-olds history without Seoul's scale. It sits just behind Kyushu because the landscape is softer and the Indian visa is still required.
distinctive: A shield volcano you do not need to summit, lava tubes, and a capital of an old kingdom scattered through green mounds.
weather: Jeju in April is mild, often the mid-teens, windy, and not beach-swimming weather. Hallasan's upper trails can still hold snow or ice. Seasonal expectation.
crowds: Early April coincides with blossom season and domestic travel. Mid-April is kinder. Jeju's big sights have car-park crowds on weekends. Gyeongju is calmer than Seoul.
natureExperiences: A coastal volcanic cone such as Seongsan, without a dangerous cliff edge
A short Hallasan approach, not the summit
The green mounds of Gyeongju by bike or on foot
age6: Lava tube, folk village, beach walks, and the tumuli park. No Hallasan summit.
age12: The lava-tube geology and the idea of a kingdom you can still see in the landscape.
age14: Gyeongju's museum, plus the science museum or a planetarium if you add a short Seoul buffer. This plan keeps Seoul optional.
adults: Food, a walkable history city, and an island that is not a resort week.
gettingAround: Fly into Jeju. A car, or two, on the island. Then a flight to Busan or Seoul and a train to Gyeongju. Korea drives on the right. Trains are the easy part.
meetingPoint: Seoul or Jeju. Seoul is the easier ticket from both Bengaluru and Melbourne. A domestic hop to Jeju is about an hour. Indian passports need a visa. Australian passports were inside a K-ETA exemption through 31 December 2026. From 1 January 2027 that exemption was described as ending, so April 2027 likely needs a K-ETA. Recheck the official K-ETA site.
visaAu: Short tourism stays have been visa-free for Australians, with K-ETA temporarily waived through 31 December 2026. Plan on a K-ETA for April 2027 unless Korea extends the waiver. Children have had age exemptions from K-ETA in past notices. Read the current rule for each traveller.
visaIn: Indian passports are not K-ETA eligible. The Korean consulate in Mumbai states that Indian nationals need a visa. Apply through the official mission.
disadvantages: Hallasan's summit is the wrong goal with a 6-year-old in April.
The scenery is lovely and less dramatic than Aso, Fiordland or Jiuzhaigou.
Blossom week and weekends are the busy times.
Two passport processes: a visa and, likely, a K-ETA.
uncertainties: Which Hallasan trails are open in April 2027.
Jeju car supply for a group of seven.

gain: An easy, kind, educational fortnight the children will find simple to enjoy.
miss: The dramatic landscape of the top nature picks.

cost.summary: Melbourne to Jeju is about ₹1.6–2.6 lakh for three adult returns. Bengaluru to Seoul, the easier meeting airport, is about ₹1.8–2.6 lakh for four. The hop from Seoul to Jeju is not included. The Korean visa fee was not priced.

lines.text: Kayak.com.au’s typical return fare, Melbourne to Jeju, was A$789–$1,327 for one adult, with one stop. Three adult fares are about ₹1.6–2.6 lakh. Not an April 2027 quote.

Kayak.co.in’s typical return fare, Bengaluru to Seoul Incheon, was ₹46,053–₹65,187 for one adult. Four adult fares are about ₹1.8–2.6 lakh. Seoul is the meeting airport in the plan. A separate Bengaluru–Jeju typical fare was not used. Not an April 2027 quote.
Indian passports need a Korean visa. The fee was not read from an official table in this pass. The Australian K-ETA rule for April 2027 still has to be rechecked, so no fee is shown.

cost.leftOut: Hotels, meals, the hop to Jeju and tickets are not included.

trip.band: about ₹6–18 lakh before the island hop and the visa
trip.note: Flights from Melbourne to Jeju and from Bengaluru to Seoul are inside this. The Seoul–Jeju hop and the Korean visa fee are not.
trip.text: A band for seven people and about 13 nights, rounded to the nearest lakh. Not a quote, and not used to order the list. Three rooms, meals for seven, local transport and tickets. The 6-year-old's meals are not discounted. Insurance, bags and shopping are outside it. The low end is Jeju's budget column and the high end is Seoul's mid-range column, because the plan also uses a mainland city.

stretch16: Add a free beach-walk day on Jeju and a free day in Gyeongju. Seoul only if the flight requires it.

days.experience: Fly to the island and walk a harbour town.
days.optional: Black pork or seafood for the adults, rice and noodles for the cautious
days.transfer: Seoul to Jeju is often about an hour. Confirm the meeting city.

days.kids: All three. It is cool, dark and flat enough. Take a layer.
days.transfer: Driving on the east of the island. Allow the morning.
days.seasonal: The tube is the science highlight. Confirm it is open.
days.wet: The tube is the wet-weather plan.

days.experience: Seongsan Ilchulbong from the safer paths, and a folk village.
days.optional: Sunrise only if everyone wants a 5am start. Mid-morning is fine.
days.highlight: A tuff cone above the sea
days.kids: Stay behind rails. The village is the 6-year-old's half of the day.
days.seasonal: Wind on the cone can be the reason to stay below.

days.experience: A beach walk and a free afternoon. No summit.
days.optional: A waterfall viewed from the path
days.kids: The sea is cold. Looking is the activity.
days.seasonal: Hallasan summit stays off the plan.
days.wet: A science museum or aquarium. Confirm what is open in 2027 before you promise a name.

days.experience: A free day or a short Hallasan trailhead visit without going up.
days.seasonal: If a lower trail is icy, do not start.

days.experience: Fly north and train to Gyeongju.
days.optional: The tumuli park at dusk if you arrive in time
days.highlight: Burial mounds sitting in a living city
days.kids: The mounds are strange and immediate. That is enough for day one.
days.transfer: Jeju to Busan or Seoul, then train. Busan is the shorter onward train. Confirm 2027 connections for seven.
days.seasonal: Do not spend the connection night in Seoul unless the flight forces it.

days.experience: Daereungwon tombs and the national museum.
days.optional: Cheomseongdae observatory, a short outdoor stop
days.highlight: A kingdom you can still read in the grass
days.kids: Museum for an hour. Park for as long as they run.
days.transfer: In town, on foot or by the local bikes and taxis.
days.seasonal: Blossom, if any remains, will be busy. The mounds are the point.

days.experience: Bulguksa temple and Seokguram only if the group wants a longer day.
days.optional: Stop at the temple and skip the upper grotto
days.highlight: A mountain temple and a stone Buddha in a cave
days.kids: Temple courtyards suit all three. The grotto walk is the optional extra.
days.transfer: A short bus or taxi out of town.
days.wet: Stay with the museum and the tomb park.

days.experience: A free day. Bikes around the mounds or a hanok stay afternoon.
days.kids: Bikes if the rental is safe for the ages you have.
days.seasonal: This is the day that makes two weeks feel kind.

days.experience: Move to the international airport with a buffer.
days.optional: One market, not a palace list
days.highlight: Leaving without adding a third destination
days.transfer: Gyeongju to Seoul is a few hours by train. To Busan it is shorter. Pick the airport that has the long-haul seats.
days.seasonal: A buffer matters more than a last palace.
